pages.title: Services
pages.content:
Services

Everything the workshop does

Hayate Cycles is the workshop at Kanaalstraat 27, 9000 Ghent, opened in 2012 by Lena Vos and Samir Haddad. Six jobs cover the bench, from a new bike to a winter e-bike check.

01

New bikes

For commuters and weekend riders who want a bike from this floor. The house line is Hayate: the City 8 at €980, the Gravel 2×10 at €1,640, and the E-City Step-Through at €2,890. Each new bike includes a free fit session, which is €160 if you book it on its own, and free local delivery within 10 km of Kanaalstraat 27. Grace Okonkwo looks after new bikes on the shop floor. We build them up here and stand behind the work with the same written quote we use for every other job. Parts you add later ship to Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg for a flat €7.50. Come in Tue–Fri 09:00–18:30 or Sat 09:00–17:00, or call +32 9 555 01 27.

See the shop

02

Bike fitting

For commuters and weekend riders who want the contact points set to their position, not to a guess. Tomás Ferreira runs the fit: a 90-minute session covering saddle, reach and cleats, with a written fit sheet at the end. The price is €160 by appointment, and it is free when you buy a new bike from the shop. The session is a measurement and a setup. It is not a statement about speed, comfort outcomes or health. Book it by calling the workshop, emailing hello@hayate-cycles.example, or asking at the desk. Mei-Ling Chen handles bookings. The bike stays with you; you ride it home on the position written on the sheet.

Bike fitting

03

Tune-ups

For commuters who ride most days and want the bike checked before something fails on the way to work. A basic tune-up is €69 and covers gears, brakes, a wheel true, a chain clean and a bolt check, ready within 2 working days. A full service is €149: the bike is stripped, cleaned, bearings are regreased, cables are replaced, and the full tune-up is done, also within 2 working days. Jonas Becker does repairs and tune-ups. Drop-off starts with a free 15-minute safety check of brakes, tyres, chain, bolts and lights, and a written note. You get a written quote before any work. Nothing is added beyond that quote without a phone call.

Tune-ups

04

Repairs

For commuters and weekend riders with a specific fault. A puncture repair is €15 for the labour, with the tube or tyre extra, and it is done while you wait. Wheel trueing is €20 per wheel, with spoke tension balanced, and it is done the same day. Any small fix that takes under 30 minutes is done while you wait. Anything longer goes on the bench and comes back within the time on the quote. You leave with a short note of what was done. If an adjustment needs redoing, we redo it free within 30 days. Book online, call +32 9 555 01 27, or bring the bike to Kanaalstraat 27, 9000 Ghent.

Repairs

05

Wheels

For riders whose wheel no longer tracks straight, and for anyone who wants a wheel built at this bench. Lena Vos, co-founder and head mechanic, is the wheel builder. A wheel true is €20 per wheel, same day, with spoke tension balanced. A wheel build is €90 labour per wheel, hand-laced and tensioned, ready in 5 working days. The Hand-built Wheelset 32h, a pair of 32-spoke wheels, is €540 on the floor. The quote names the labour and any rim, spokes or hub before work starts. A wheel that has been adjusted is covered by the same 30-day rule as the rest of the workshop: if the adjustment needs redoing, it is redone free.

Wheels

06

E-bike care

For e-bike owners. An e-bike service is €119 and takes 2 working days. It includes the basic tune-up plus a motor and battery diagnostic, firmware and a check of the connectors. Samir Haddad, co-founder, looks after e-bikes and electrics. He also keeps a short winter list for e-cargo bikes: connectors, battery storage and brake pads. The visit starts like any other, with the free 15-minute safety check and a written quote. Firmware and diagnostic work stay inside that quote. If the motor needs more than the quoted time, Samir calls before he continues. Pick-up includes a short note of what was checked and what was changed.

E-bike service

Every job starts with a free 15-minute safety check of brakes, tyres, chain, bolts and lights, and a written note. The full price list is one page away.

See the prices

pages.title: Shop
pages.content:
Shop

Bikes we build up and stand behind

Grace Okonkwo runs the shop floor at Kanaalstraat 27. The bikes and parts here are the Hayate house line, priced in euro, with a free fit on every new bike.

01

City

The Hayate City 8 is €980. It is the house city bike: olive-grey, with mudguards and a rack, for the ride to work along the canal and the streets around Ghent. Grace Okonkwo looks after new bikes on the shop floor and can walk you through what is built up and ready. A new bike includes a free fit session with Tomás Ferreira. Booked on its own, that session is €160 and lasts 90 minutes. Local delivery is free within 10 km. The City 8 is sold from Kanaalstraat 27 during shop hours, Tue–Fri 09:00–18:30 and Sat 09:00–17:00. Sunday and Monday the shop is closed.

02

Gravel

The Hayate Gravel 2×10 is €1,640. It is the house gravel bike: graphite, with wide tyres, geared 2×10, for weekend rides that leave the city. The Saturday shop ride, 45 km at 07:30, no-drop and free, is the kind of morning this bike is built up for. Elif Yıldız leads that ride. The same new-bike terms apply: a free fit session, and free delivery within 10 km. Grace Okonkwo can set one aside on the floor if you call ahead. The price on the floor is the bike. A later wheel build, a tune-up or a replacement part is quoted on its own before any work.

03

E-bikes

The Hayate E-City Step-Through is €2,890. It is the house step-through e-bike, stone in colour, with an integrated battery, for commuters who want a motor in the same kind of bike they would otherwise pedal. Samir Haddad looks after e-bikes and electrics once it is on the road. An e-bike service, when you need one, is €119 and includes a basic tune-up, a motor and battery diagnostic, firmware and the connectors, ready within 2 working days. The bike itself includes the free fit session and free delivery within 10 km. We do not quote a range, and we do not say how far a charge will carry you.

04

Wheels and parts

The Hand-built Wheelset 32h is €540. It is a pair of hand-built 32-spoke wheels from Lena Vos’s bench. Buying the pair is different from booking a wheel build: the build is labour at €90 per wheel, hand-laced and tensioned, in 5 working days, and the wheelset is the finished pair on the floor. A wheel true, if you already have wheels, is €20 per wheel, same day. Parts you order rather than fit in the shop ship to Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg for a flat €7.50. The shipping price is the same on a small part as on a larger one. It is not a per-kilo rate.

05

Accessories

The Commuter Light Set is €65. It is a front and rear light pair for the dark months on the canal path, the same kind of lights the free safety check looks at when you drop a bike off. Lights, and any other accessory, ship to BE, NL and LU for €7.50. A light set is not a bike, so the free fit session and the 10 km delivery apply only to new bikes. Grace Okonkwo can add the set to a City 8, a Gravel 2×10 or an E-City Step-Through before the bike leaves. If you only need the lights, take them from the floor or have them posted.

New bikes include a free fit session · Free delivery within 10 km of the shop · Parts ship to Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg for a flat €7.50.

Come and see them

pages.title: Bike fitting
pages.content:
Service

Bike fitting

Tomás Ferreira fits saddles, reach and cleats in a 90-minute session at the workshop. The price is €160, and the session is free with a new bike.

The session

90 minutes · €160 · free with a new bike

Tomás Ferreira is the bike fitter at Hayate Cycles. A fit is a 90-minute appointment at €160, and it is included when you buy a new bike. You leave with a written fit sheet that records saddle, reach and cleats. The session is for commuters and weekend riders who want those three points set and written down. It is a workshop appointment, not a medical visit, and it comes with no stated result. Book by phone on +32 9 555 01 27, by email at hello@hayate-cycles.example, or through Mei-Ling Chen at the desk. Hours are Tue–Fri 09:00–18:30 and Sat 09:00–17:00. The shop is closed Sunday and Monday.

Five stages

What happens on the day

01

Interview

The first stage is a conversation before anyone reaches for a tool. Tomás asks what you ride, how long the rides are, and whether the bike is for the daily trip or for the weekend. A commuter riding 16 km each way is a different setup from a Saturday 45 km shop ride, and he writes that down before measuring. Tell him which bike you will actually use. If the bike is a new Hayate City 8, Gravel 2×10 or E-City Step-Through, the session is already included. If it is your own bike, the €160 covers this interview and the four stages after it. The sheet starts here, with the riding you came in to describe.

02

Flexibility check

The second stage is a flexibility check on the bike, indoors, so the later numbers have a starting point. Tomás looks at how you sit and how far you can reach without forcing a position you cannot hold. He does not turn that into a health claim, a treatment or a score. It is a check so the saddle and the bars are set somewhere you can use on a real ride, whether that ride is the canal path into Ghent or a longer weekend on the gravel bike. If something about the bike, rather than the position, needs the workshop, he stops and the job becomes a quote with Jonas Becker, not a quiet change during the fit.

03

Saddle height and setback

The third stage sets saddle height and setback. Tomás measures, moves the saddle, and writes the figure on the fit sheet so it can be put back if the post slips or the bike is serviced later. There is no standard change. One rider’s sheet is not the next rider’s. When the saddle is where it will stay, he checks that the clamps are tight, which is the same bolt check the free 15-minute safety check covers at a workshop drop-off. If an adjustment from the session needs redoing, the workshop redoes it free within 30 days. Bring the sheet with you if you come back.

04

Reach and bars

The fourth stage is reach and the bars. Tomás shortens or lengthens the position and records it. A change can be small. In one session he shortened the reach on Marco’s gravel bike by 20 mm; that figure belonged to Marco’s bike and his sheet, and it is not a target for anyone else. The point of the stage is the same for every rider: the reach you leave with is written down, and the bars match it. Weekend riders often use this stage before a longer ride. Commuters use it when the daily position has been a guess since the day the bike was bought.

05

Cleats and test ride

The fifth stage sets the cleats, if you ride with them, and finishes with a test ride. Tomás checks the cleat position, you ride, and he adjusts once more if the ride shows something the indoor check did not. The sheet is completed after that ride, not before. You take the sheet home. The fit does not include a tune-up, a wheel true or a drivetrain replacement unless those were quoted separately. A basic tune-up is €69, a wheel true is €20 per wheel, and both go through the usual rule: written quote first, and a phone call before anything beyond it. Book the fit on its own, or take it free with a new bike.

A fit is €160 for 90 minutes by appointment, and free when you buy a new bike from the shop. It ends with a written fit sheet.

Book a fit

pages.title: Repairs and tune-ups
pages.content:
Service

Repairs and tune-ups

Jonas Becker handles repairs and tune-ups. Samir Haddad handles e-bikes and electrics. Every job starts with a free safety check and a written quote.

01

Basic tune-up

The basic tune-up is €69. Jonas Becker does the work: gears, brakes, a wheel true, a chain clean and a bolt check. It is ready within 2 working days. This is the visit most commuters book when the bike has been ridden all season and nothing is actually broken. It starts, like every drop-off, with a free 15-minute safety check. Brakes, tyres, chain, bolts and lights are looked at, and you get a written note. If the check shows more than a tune-up, you get a written quote before that extra work starts. Nothing is added beyond the quote without a phone call. You pick the bike up with a short note of what was done.

02

Full service

The full service is €149, ready within 2 working days. The bike is stripped and cleaned, the bearings are regreased, the cables are replaced, and the full tune-up is done on top of that. Jonas Becker carries this one when a basic tune-up is no longer the right size of job: a bike that has done a long stretch of daily riding, or a winter’s worth of wet paths. Parts named in the quote are the parts that get replaced. A chain, a cassette or chainrings are extra when they are extra, and they appear on the quote before they are ordered. The 30-day rule applies to adjustments: if one needs redoing, it is redone free within 30 days.

03

E-bike service

The e-bike service is €119 and is ready within 2 working days. It is the basic tune-up plus a motor and battery diagnostic, firmware, and a check of the connectors. Samir Haddad looks after e-bikes and electrics, including the Hayate E-City Step-Through and e-cargo bikes that come in for winter. His checklist for an e-cargo bike through the cold months is three items: connectors, battery storage and brake pads. Connectors are checked seated and clean. The battery is discussed as a storage question, off the bike when it will sit. Brake pads are inspected because a loaded cargo bike uses them. The diagnostic stays inside the written quote. If firmware or the motor needs more time, Samir calls first.

Book, drop off, quote

How a job goes through the workshop

The visit has five steps, and they stay in this order. You book online or call +32 9 555 01 27. You drop the bike off and it gets the free 15-minute safety check, with a written note. You receive a written quote, and nothing beyond that quote is done without a phone call. The workshop does the work and a test ride. You pick the bike up with a short note of what was done. Mei-Ling Chen at the service desk takes the booking. The shop is at Kanaalstraat 27, 9000 Ghent, open Tue–Fri 09:00–18:30 and Sat 09:00–17:00, closed Sunday and Monday. Email hello@hayate-cycles.example if you would rather write than call.

01Book online or call

02Drop-off and a free 15-minute safety check

03A written quote, nothing extra without a call

04The work and a test ride

05Pick-up with a short note of what was done

While you wait

Repairs and the 30-day rule

Repairs

Punctures and other small fixes are done while you wait when the job is under 30 minutes. A puncture repair is €15 in labour. The tube or the tyre is extra if it needs replacing. A wheel true is €20 per wheel, spoke tension balanced, and it is done the same day, which may be longer than a wait at the counter. Tune-ups, the full service and the e-bike service use the 2 working day window. Any adjustment is redone free within 30 days. That covers a gear, a brake or a wheel that was set here and does not hold. It is a workshop rule about our own adjustment, not a statement of how the bike will feel or how long a part will last.

See the prices

pages.title: Wheels
pages.content:
Service

Wheels

Lena Vos builds and trues wheels at the back bench. A true is €20 per wheel, same day. A build is €90 in labour per wheel, in 5 working days.

The bench Lena works at

Lena Vos, co-founder and wheel builder

Lena Vos is co-founder, head mechanic and the wheel builder. She works at the long bench at the back of the former print shop at Kanaalstraat 27, which she and Samir Haddad opened in 2012. A wheel is the job she will not rush past. The shop’s standard for itself is plain: a bike leaves running true. That means the rim tracks, the spoke tension is balanced, and the wheel is ridden in the stand before it goes back to the street. It does not speak to your riding. Commuters bring city wheels that have picked up a wobble on the canal path. Weekend riders bring wheels that have done a season of gravel. Both sit in the same stand, under the same task lamp.

A rear wheel, 36 spokes

One rebuild on this bench was a 1980s steel touring wheel. Lena rebuilt it onto a new rim with 36 spokes, hand-tensioned, so the wheel would run true again. The rim was new. The spoke count stayed at 36 because that was the wheel she was rebuilding. The work was quoted before she started, like every other job in the room. A wheel build of that kind is labour, and the labour price is €90 per wheel, hand-laced and tensioned, ready in 5 working days. The rim, spokes and hub are named on the quote if they are not already in your wheel. Nothing is added after the quote without a phone call.

Three wheel jobs

Prices are labour per wheel

01

Wheel true

A wheel true is €20 per wheel. Spoke tension is balanced, and the work is done the same day. Bring the wheel, or the whole bike, during shop hours. The free 15-minute safety check still happens at drop-off if the bike comes in, and you still get a written note. A true is an adjustment. If it needs redoing, it is redone free within 30 days. If the rim is too far out for a true, Lena says so before any further work and writes a quote for a build instead. Same-day means the day you bring it in, inside Tue–Fri 09:00–18:30 or Sat 09:00–17:00. Sunday and Monday the workshop is closed.

Prices

02

Wheel build

A wheel build is €90 in labour per wheel. Lena laces it by hand and tensions it, and the wheel is ready in 5 working days. The price is the labour. Parts are extra and are written into the quote before she starts. A pair is two wheels, so two labour charges, unless you are buying the finished Hand-built Wheelset 32h from the floor instead. Use a build when you already know the rim and hub you want, or when a wheel can be trued no further. Book it the same way as any workshop job: online, by phone on +32 9 555 01 27, or by email at hello@hayate-cycles.example. You pick it up with a short note of what was done.

Prices

03

Hand-built Wheelset 32h

The Hand-built Wheelset 32h is €540. It is a pair of hand-built 32-spoke wheels, sold as a floor product rather than as a labour line. Lena builds wheels; this is the pair the shop keeps ready. It sits with the house bikes: the City 8 at €980, the Gravel 2×10 at €1,640 and the E-City Step-Through at €2,890. If the pair is posted rather than fitted here, parts and accessories ship to Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg for a flat €7.50. Fitting it to a bike in the workshop is a separate quoted job. A new bike’s free fit session covers saddle, reach and cleats. It does not replace a wheel invoice.

Shop

pages.title: Prices
pages.content:
Workshop

Prices

Eight jobs, priced in euro, identical on the floor and on this page. A written quote comes before any work, and adjustments are redone free within 30 days.

01

Safety check, puncture, wheel true

Safety check, free, 15 minutes. It covers brakes, tyres, chain, bolts and lights, and you leave the check with a written note. It is done at drop-off, before any paid work. Puncture repair, €15, while you wait. The price is labour. A tube or a tyre is extra if it has to be replaced. Small fixes under 30 minutes are done while you wait. Wheel true, €20 per wheel, same day. Spoke tension is balanced. If a wheel needs more than a true, you get a quote for that extra work and a phone call before it starts. These three are the short visits. They still follow the workshop rule that nothing proceeds on assumption.

02

Basic tune-up, e-bike service, full service

Basic tune-up, €69, ready within 2 working days. It includes gears, brakes, a wheel true, a chain clean and a bolt check. E-bike service, €119, ready within 2 working days. It includes the basic tune-up plus a motor and battery diagnostic, firmware and the connectors. Full service, €149, ready within 2 working days. The bike is stripped and cleaned, the bearings are regreased, the cables are replaced, and the full tune-up is done. Jonas Becker carries the tune-ups and repairs. Samir Haddad carries the e-bike diagnostic and the electrics. All three start with the free safety check and a written quote. Parts that are not in the line above are written as extras before anyone fits them.

03

Bike fit and wheel build

Bike fit, €160, by appointment. The session is 90 minutes and covers saddle, reach and cleats. You leave with a written fit sheet. Tomás Ferreira does the fit. It is free when you buy a new bike: the Hayate City 8 at €980, the Hayate Gravel 2×10 at €1,640, or the Hayate E-City Step-Through at €2,890. Wheel build, €90 labour per wheel, hand-laced and tensioned, ready in 5 working days. Lena Vos builds the wheel. The Hand-built Wheelset 32h, the finished pair, is a separate product at €540. Labour and the product are not the same line. A build quote lists parts on their own if the wheel is not the stock pair.

What the price does not hide

You get a written quote before any work. Parts are extra when the table says they are extra, and when a worn part has to be replaced for the job to make sense. A chain, a cassette and chainrings are a common example on a bike that has been ridden every day: they go on the quote, and they are not fitted until you have agreed by phone if they were not in the first figure. Any adjustment is redone free within 30 days. New bikes include the fit. New bikes also include free local delivery within 10 km. Parts and accessories ship to Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg for a flat €7.50. Prices are in euro. The note records the work that was done, and nothing past that note.

Book a service

pages.title: Rides
pages.content:
Rides

Rides

Two free meetings leave from the shop. The Saturday ride is 45 km at 07:30, no-drop. The commuter clinic is the first Wednesday of the month at 19:00, with 12 places.

Saturday shop ride

07:30 · 45 km · no-drop · free

The shop ride leaves every Saturday at 07:30 from Kanaalstraat 27. It is 45 km, no-drop, and free. Elif Yıldız, apprentice mechanic, leads it. No-drop means the group keeps the last rider in sight and waits. The pace is a weekend ride, not a race, and nobody has to belong to a club to roll out. You bring your own bike, in the state you are willing to ride 45 km. If the bike needs a look before Saturday, book a safety check or a tune-up earlier in the week. The check is free and takes 15 minutes. The workshop is closed on Sunday and Monday, so a bike left on Saturday afternoon waits until Tuesday. Meet at the shop. The ride starts on time.

01

Commuter clinic

The commuter clinic is on the first Wednesday of the month at 19:00. It is free, and there are 12 places. It is for people who ride to work and want an hour on the things that stop a weekday ride: a soft tyre, a light that has failed, a gear that jumps, a bolt that has worked loose. It is not a full service. A full service is €149 and takes 2 working days on the bench. The clinic is a short session in the evening, after the shop’s 18:30 close on a normal Wednesday, held because commuters cannot always come in the middle of the day. Mei-Ling Chen at the desk keeps the list of 12. When the list is full, the next clinic is the following month.

First Wednesday of the month · 19:00 · 12 places · free

02

Who the rides are for

The Saturday ride is the weekend side of the shop. The clinic is the commuter side. Both are free, and neither is a lesson you pay for or a result held out in advance. Riders on the Saturday group are out for 45 km. Riders at the clinic are getting a bike ready for the morning after. Elif leads the weekend ride. The mechanics, Jonas Becker on repairs and Lena Vos on wheels, are in the workshop during the week if the clinic shows something that needs a quote. An e-bike question goes to Samir Haddad. A position question goes to Tomás Ferreira and, if you want it properly done, to the €160 fit. The rides themselves stay free.

03

Before you roll out

Bring a bike with working brakes and a rear light if you will be out near dusk. The canal path is the way a lot of Ghent riders already use, and the shop ride uses the roads beyond it for the 45 km. There is parking for 12 bikes in front of the shop if you arrive early and want to leave a lock for later. The shop itself is open Saturday 09:00–17:00, which is after the 07:30 start, so the ride meets outside even when the door is still shut. Call +32 9 555 01 27 or email hello@hayate-cycles.example if you want a clinic place. For the Saturday ride, come to the door at 07:30. Elif will be there.

Visit the shop

pages.title: A workshop on the Kanaalstraat since 2012
pages.content:
About

A workshop on the Kanaalstraat since 2012

Lena Vos and Samir Haddad opened Hayate Cycles in 2012 in a former print shop on the Kanaalstraat. The tall window and the long back bench are still how the place is arranged.

A former print shop

Kanaalstraat 27, Ghent

Hayate Cycles opened in 2012. Lena Vos, a mechanic, and Samir Haddad, an electrician who became a mechanic, took a former print shop at Kanaalstraat 27, 9000 Ghent. The tall street window is still the front of the shop. The long workbench is still at the back, which is where wheels are built and where a bike sits when a tune-up takes the 2 working days on the card. For everything practical it is the place on the page: the door for drop-off, the meeting point for the Saturday 07:30 ride, and the desk where Mei-Ling Chen answers the phone, +32 9 555 01 27, and hello@hayate-cycles.example.

01

Why every wheel gets trued

A bike goes back to the street running true, or it does not go back yet. That is the workshop’s standard, and it is why a wheel true sits in the basic tune-up as well as on its own line at €20 per wheel. Lena Vos would rather spend the time in the stand than hand back a wheel that pulls. The same idea covers the rest of the job. You get a written quote before work starts. You get a phone call if the job needs to grow. You get a short note at pick-up. If an adjustment needs redoing, it is redone free within 30 days. None of this speaks to how fast you will ride, how a knee will feel, or how many seasons a part will last. It is about the work on the note.

02

What we will not sell you

The floor sells the Hayate house line and the parts the workshop builds or fits. The bikes are the City 8 at €980, the Gravel 2×10 at €1,640 and the E-City Step-Through at €2,890. The pair of wheels is the Hand-built Wheelset 32h at €540. The light pair is the Commuter Light Set at €65. Frames and components are unbranded or Hayate. The shop does not borrow another maker’s name to fill a shelf. It also does not sell a stated result. A fit sheet records a position. A service note records what was done. A quote records the price you agreed. If you want a different bike from the three on the floor, the honest answer is that this is the range.

The seven people

Lena Vos, co-founder, head mechanic and wheel builder, works the wheel stand. Samir Haddad, co-founder, looks after e-bikes and electrics. Tomás Ferreira is the bike fitter, on appointment, at €160 for 90 minutes. Grace Okonkwo is on the shop floor with the new bikes. Jonas Becker is the mechanic for repairs and tune-ups. Mei-Ling Chen runs the service desk and the bookings. Elif Yıldız is the apprentice mechanic and leads the Saturday ride. Seven people, one bench, one desk, one door on the Kanaalstraat. If you are not sure who you need, start with Mei-Ling. She will put a repair with Jonas, a wheel with Lena, an e-bike with Samir, a fit with Tomás, or a new bike with Grace.

pages.title: Visit
pages.content:
Visit

Visit

The shop and workshop are at Kanaalstraat 27, 9000 Ghent. Mei-Ling Chen is at the desk for bookings, drop-offs and pick-ups.

01

Address, phone, email

Hayate Cycles, Kanaalstraat 27, 9000 Ghent, Belgium. Phone +32 9 555 01 27. Email hello@hayate-cycles.example. The shop and the workshop are the same door. New bikes are on the floor inside the tall street window. The bench is at the back. Come in for a bike, a fit, a repair or a question about the Saturday ride. If you are dropping a bike for work, the free 15-minute safety check happens at that drop-off, and you do not need a separate appointment for the check itself. You do need an appointment for a bike fit, and you need a booking if you want one of the 12 places at the commuter clinic. Mei-Ling Chen is at the desk.

Kanaalstraat 27, 9000 Ghent · +32 9 555 01 27 · hello@hayate-cycles.example

02

Hours

Tuesday to Friday, 09:00–18:30. Saturday, 09:00–17:00. Sunday and Monday, closed. The Saturday shop ride leaves at 07:30, before the door opens for ordinary shop hours, and meets outside. The commuter clinic is the first Wednesday of the month at 19:00, after the usual 18:30 close, and it is listed separately because it is not a late opening of the shop floor. A tune-up dropped on Friday still follows the 2 working day rule, which counts the days the workshop is open. A wheel build is 5 working days. If you need a puncture repaired while you wait, come inside the hours above. A job under 30 minutes can be done then. The phone is answered in those hours.

03

How to book

Call, email, or drop in. Mei-Ling Chen takes bookings at the service desk. A workshop job can also be booked online. Say which bike, and say whether you want a basic tune-up at €69, a full service at €149, an e-bike service at €119, a wheel true at €20 per wheel, a wheel build at €90 labour per wheel, or a fit at €160. If you are not sure, book the drop-off and the safety check. The quote will name the work before anything is taken apart. Nothing beyond the quote is done without a phone call, so leave a number that reaches you during the 2 working days. Pick-up is at the same desk. You get a short note of what was done.

04

Getting here

The shop is on the canal side of Ghent, and the canal path is the way most people arrive by bike. There is parking for 12 bikes in front of the window. Lock to the stands and come in; the floor is not a public rack beyond those 12. If you are driving a bike to us because it cannot be ridden, the drop-off is the same door. Free local delivery of a new bike runs within 10 km, which covers a new Hayate bought here and sent home, not a repair collected from across the city. Parts and accessories posted to Belgium, the Netherlands or Luxembourg are €7.50 flat. For a repair, the usual way home is to ride it. The test ride is done before you pick up.

posts.title: Eight thousand kilometres to work
posts.excerpt: After two years of riding 16 km each way along the canal, Ines brought her bike to Jonas Becker for a chain, a cassette and chainrings.
posts.content:
Ines starts early. The ride to work is 16 km each way along the canal, and she has ridden it on ordinary working days for two years. The path is the flat way across Ghent. The wind is the part that changes. In the dark months the rear light is on before she leaves. In the light months she is at her desk with the ride already behind her. Hayate Cycles stands on that canal side of the city, at Kanaalstraat 27, in a former print shop with a tall street window. After two years, the bike came back to a bench that sees this kind of distance often.

Eight thousand kilometres is what those mornings and evenings added up to. The chain had stretched. A shift onto the smaller cogs took a moment longer than it used to. The chainrings showed a hooked tooth where the chain had sat, morning out and evening back. Ines booked a basic tune-up. The basic tune-up is €69 and covers gears, brakes, a wheel true, a chain clean and a bolt check, ready within 2 working days. Jonas Becker, the mechanic who does repairs and tune-ups, took the bike in and asked her to leave it for a proper look. He did not start replacing parts on the strength of the first booking.

The workshop rule is the same for a commuter bike as for any other. Drop-off includes a free 15-minute safety check. Brakes, tyres, chain, bolts and lights are looked at, and the check ends with a written note. Any work beyond that waits for a written quote. Anything beyond the quote waits for a phone call. Jonas rang the same afternoon. The chain, the cassette and the chainrings had worn as a set, which is what two years of daily riding usually does. A new chain on the old rings would have repeated the noise within a short time. He read the extras out, waited until Ines said yes, and only then put the parts on the job.

The bike used the 2 working days. Worn parts came off. The new chain, the new cassette and the new chainrings went on together. Jonas cleaned the bike and set the gears so the new chain sat where it should. He checked the wheels and left them true enough for the canal path. A puncture or a small fix would have been done while she waited, if it had taken under 30 minutes. A puncture is €15 in labour, with the tube or tyre extra. This was not that visit. A drivetrain with eight thousand kilometres on it is a bench job.

Ines collected the bike from Mei-Ling Chen at the service desk and took the short note that leaves with every job. The note said what had been done. It did not say she would arrive at work sooner, or that the ride would feel different in any particular way. She rode the first stretch behind the shop and turned onto the canal. The shift was quiet. The chain sat. The next morning she left at the usual time, for the same 16 km.

She still rides alone on weekdays. The shop ride is there if she wants it: every Saturday at 07:30, 45 km, no-drop, free, led by Elif Yıldız. The weekday trip is the one the bike was wearing out on, and it is the one the new parts are for. When something starts to tick, she knows the number, +32 9 555 01 27, and the address. If an adjustment from the visit needs redoing, the workshop redoes it free within 30 days. That rule is about the work Jonas did, not about how long a chain will last the next time.

Lena Vos and Samir Haddad opened the shop in 2012. The long bench at the back is still where a job like this one sits, under the task lamp, until the note is written and the bike can go back to the street. Ines does not need the history of the building. She needs the quote before the parts, the phone call before any extra line, and a bike that will do the canal again tomorrow. After two years and eight thousand kilometres, that is what she rode home with.
